title: North Yemen
capsule: North Yemen across 1919–1990 spans two distinct regimes in the Zaydi highlands centred on Sana'a. From 1918, when Imam Yahya Hamid ed-Din entered Sana'a after the Ottoman withdrawal, the Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen ruled as an isolationist Islamic monarchy; Yahya lost Najran, Asir and Jizan to Saudi Arabia in 1934 and was assassinated in 1948, after which his son Ahmad reigned until 1962. In September 1962 republican army officers under Abdullah al-Sallal overthrew the newly enthroned Imam al-Badr and proclaimed the Yemen Arab Republic, igniting an eight-year civil war in which Egyptian troops backed the republicans against Saudi-supported royalists. The republic later consolidated under Ali Abdullah Saleh (from 1978) and merged with South Yemen on 22 May 1990 to form the unified Republic of Yemen.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial extent of North Yemen is clearly defined by the 1934 Treaty of Taif boundary with Saudi Arabia and the 1990 unification border; attestation is strong for the twentieth-century period.
